title: Walks that fail in the full sweep
goal: The scripted walks are the app driving itself, and some of them no longer reach what they were written to check. Find out what each failing walk is looking for, then either fix the app if the walk is right or update the walk if the app moved on. This serves the focus because the sweep is the only thing that tells a focus runner whether the change it just made broke anything: a sweep with failures nobody has named cannot say that, so every focus feature ships on a weaker claim than it should.

log.note: triage 2026-09-27: moved to p1 because transition-picker-at-a-cut-walk, a focus walk, is among the 8. Grouped by cause from queue/sweep/2026-09-27-023556.log: (1) panel-rows-read-as-one-column-walk, transition-picker-at-a-cut-walk and video-panel-order-walk all fail the panelMargins check on 'Window title (<name> · 1280 x 800 · 0:08 · saved)', the title bar line 943c406d added, which the check now counts as a panel item (runs 936 to 1464pt past the panel's left edge). Reproduced by triage: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/video-panel-order-walk.json --no-build exits 1, /tmp/photonz-playtest/video-panel-order-walk/panel-margins-1-a-clip.json has exactly those two breaches. Likely fix is in the margins check (skip items outside the dock), not the app. (2) opacity-on-a-video-shape-walk (Opacity reads 24, not 28) and pick-leaves-settings-alone-walk (Thickness reads 26, not 25): a panel value one or a few steps off, maybe the new real drags landing a pixel differently. (3) bar-end-follows-the-pointer-walk: trackRow built 65 times, the walk allows 60; its audit already says the panel rebuilds about 35 times in 40 drag moves.

owns these walks: bar-end-follows-the-pointer-walk, opacity-on-a-video-shape-walk, panel-rows-read-as-one-column-walk, pick-leaves-settings-alone-walk, transition-picker-at-a-cut-walk, video-panel-order-walk

Cause 1, the check was wrong (panel-rows-read-as-one-column, transition-picker-at-a-cut, video-panel-order): the title bar line from 943c406d spans the whole window and its bottom dips 1pt into the panel's top, so panelMargins counted it as a panel row. Reproduced with Scripts/playtest.sh video-panel-order-walk (exit 1, 'Window title ... runs 936pt past the panel's left edge'). Fix: PanelMarginRule.belongs (middle inside the panel, tested) replaces intersects in the rule and the harness. Also fixes captions-panel-keeps-its-margins-walk, which failed the same way.

Cause 2, the walks were wrong (opacity-on-a-video-shape, pick-leaves-settings-alone): e37a8618 put each slider's name beside it, so sliders are narrower and a press at 30% (60%) of the width lands on 24 (26), not 28 (25). The app is right; expected values updated.

Cause 3, the walk was wrong (bar-end-follows-the-pointer): since e459d903 dragGrip takes the front and hands it back, which rebuilds every row; a person dragging already has the app in front. Measured: 63-65 trackRow builds without front, 55 with setup front:true (limit 60). Walk now says front:true (it already needed the Mac to itself for dragGrip).

All 6 walks pass, each run on its own twice in a row (commit ead83882). Margin check skipped window chrome that grazes the panel (PanelMarginRule.belongs, tested), which also fixes captions-panel-keeps-its-margins; two walks had slider values that moved with the narrower one-column rows; bar-end now keeps the probe in front, as a person's app is. Tests 10060 green.
